How celtic names work

Celtic names lean on lenited consonant pairs — bh, dh, gh, mh — that soften the sound, plus vowel clusters that look impossible and read musically. Irish, Welsh and Scots Gaelic each tilt differently: Welsh loves w as a vowel (Gwen, Rhys), Irish loves the -ach and -aid endings.
